findings.location: Boundaries > Always (Slots bullet: '--cleanup-orphans once before the first admission, every mode'); Tasks > docs (headless.md: 'automatic --cleanup-orphans before wait-slots')
findings.issue: The spec says when the automatic cleanup runs in two different ways, and one of them contradicts the contract. The Slots bullet runs it once before the first admission of every run. cell-contract.md > Config keys and SPEC Constraints run it 'before entering wait-slots', so only when the cap is actually full. The docs task copies the contract wording, so the docs would describe different behaviour from the code. The spec also never says whether cleanup results (removed/skipped/errors) are logged, printed or recorded anywhere, even though this is the one destructive action headless runs now take on jobs they did not start.
findings.implementation_impact: An implementer must pick one trigger. Running it on every invocation adds a full container+network listing and inspect pass (up to DOCKER_CMD_TIMEOUT per call) to every single-cell canary run. Running it only before wait-slots contradicts the frozen spec text. Whichever is picked, a test or a docs sentence will be wrong, and container removals happen silently.
findings.suggestion: State one trigger that matches the contract: once per run, the first time an admission attempt fails, before the first START wait-slots line. Require the cleanup result's removed/skipped/errors lists to go to stderr and to the waiting version's progress log, and say that a 'partial' cleanup status does not abort the run.

findings.location: Design Notes > Claims; Tasks > ps-flashlight-run.py (`daemon_slot_usage()` -> (used, counted list, ok))
findings.issue: A claim counts only while no running container carries its psm.run. But daemon_slot_usage returns only the summed slots, a 'psm.job@host=cost' list and an ok flag. It does not return the psm.run labels of the counted containers. The admission code therefore cannot decide from the same snapshot whether a claim is already represented by a running container. A second docker query, or registry reads done at a different time, opens a window where a container starts between the two reads. That container is then counted neither as a label nor as a claim (under-count, so over-admission past the host cap), or it is counted twice.
findings.implementation_impact: The cap can be exceeded under exactly the concurrency CAP-3 is meant to control. The stubbed test harness cannot express the claim-vs-container interaction at all, so AC2 and any 'claim stops counting once its container runs' test cannot be written against the specified signature.
findings.suggestion: Make daemon_slot_usage return the per-container (psm.run, psm.job, owner host, cost) tuples from one `docker ps --format` call. Specify the order under slots.lock: read the registry claims first, then take one docker snapshot, then discount the claims whose run appears in that snapshot. Add a test where a claim's run appears in the stubbed snapshot and is counted exactly once.

findings.location: Boundaries > Always (Slots: 'startup-timeout clock counts only while none of this run's own children is in flight; timeout -> no-slots for every still-queued cell')
findings.issue: The spec turns the contract's per-cell wait bound (cell-contract.md > Config keys: 'the cell waits ... for at most the startup timeout') into one run-level clock that expires every still-queued cell at once. It does not say whether that clock accumulates across separate gaps (cell 2 waits 100 s in one gap, cell 3 waits 100 s in a later gap, so the total of 200 s exceeds 180 s), or whether it resets when a cell is admitted. This deviation from the contract is not listed under Ask First or Design Notes.
findings.implementation_impact: Depending on the reading, a cell that personally waited well under the timeout can be reported no-slots. Two cells of a run would then become an infra cause that later feeds CAP-1's blocked-infra rule. Tests for the 'Own queue' and 'Foreign full' rows can pass under either reading, so the ambiguity survives review.
findings.suggestion: Define the clock per queued cell, starting when that cell first fails admission and pausing while any own child is in flight. Alternatively, keep one run clock but state that it resets on every admission and record it as a deliberate interim decision. Add an I/O row with two separated foreign-full gaps that each stay under the timeout.

findings.location: Boundaries > Always (Fail-fast bullet) and Design Notes > Trigger
findings.issue: The spec changes the contract trigger from 'the first child that exits 3' (cell-contract.md > Runner > Fail-fast) to 'an appended fail record', and justifies the change in Design Notes. Its own Ask First section says that changing a contract rule needs approval, and the spec neither flags this change as approved nor adds it to the contract. It also leaves three cases open. (a) Two children reaped in the same wait() batch: the existing run_children sorts a batch by plan order, not completion order, so the cell named in 'fail-fast after <ver>:<browser>' is decided by plan order. (b) A fail record that was appended and is followed by a child exit 2 from an in-flight child: which reason do the queued cells get? (c) Are not-run records written at trigger time or after in-flight children finish?
findings.implementation_impact: Reviewers checking the code against cell-contract.md will flag the trigger as a defect. The not-run reason string (fail-fast vs input-error) and the record order in `appended` are nondeterministic between implementations, and tests asserting the reason text are fragile.
findings.suggestion: Either get the trigger change approved and write it back into cell-contract.md > Runner, or follow the contract. State that the first trigger wins and fixes the reason. State that not-run records for still-queued cells are appended immediately at the trigger, before in-flight children are reaped. State that ties inside one reap batch follow plan order (and document that 'completion order' is approximate there).

findings.location: Boundaries > Always (Honesty law: 'run exit 3 if any fail, else 1 if any record not pass') vs Fail-fast bullet ('still exits 2') and contract Runner > Output (skipped -> exit 0)
findings.issue: The exit-code sentence is incomplete and contradicts the other rules. It omits the precedence of exit 2 (child exit 2, which the previous slice ranks above fail), of 143 (stop), and of the 'skipped' path, which exits 0 even when no-slots or not-run records were appended in the same run. Read literally, 'else 1 if any record not pass' forbids exit 0 for a run that appended no-slots records and had one skipped child, but the contract requires exit 0 with `skipped` there.
findings.implementation_impact: An implementer following this spec alone writes an exit ladder that differs from the existing run_e2e ladder and the contract, and the existing tests for skipped and exit 2 either break or are 'fixed' in the wrong direction.
findings.suggestion: Replace the sentence with the full ordered ladder: 143 stopped; 2 append error (no line) or child exit 2 (line `ran`); 3 any appended fail; 0 + `skipped` when a child skipped and no fail; 1 when any appended record is not pass (including not-run and no-slots) or nothing was appended; else 0. Add a matrix row with a skipped child plus a no-slots record.

findings.location: Design Notes > Records without a child; contract Phase timings (ps-run-layer truncates the version's progress log before wait-slots)
findings.issue: Truncation is defined only for a version that enters wait-slots ('wait-slots is recorded only when the first admission attempt failed') and for a never-started version (one DONE line). The spec does not say whether ps-run-layer truncates the log of a version admitted on its first attempt. Every child now gets --progress-append, so if nothing truncates that log, it keeps the previous run's lines, including an old DONE and old bring-up lines. That breaks the AC 'no bring-up' style assertions and the stall rule. The spec also does not say what DONE line ps-run-layer writes for a version still in wait-slots when the run is stopped (exit 143), crashes, or hits an append error. With no DONE, the run-phases.md stall rule (no line for about 3 minutes and no DONE = hung) flags those logs forever.
findings.implementation_impact: Stale lines from earlier runs leak into logs read as current, which is the problem contract Phase timings exists to prevent. Orchestrators following the stall rule report phantom hangs after every stopped run.
findings.suggestion: Require ps-run-layer to truncate every queued version's log at run start, before cleanup and admission, whether or not it later waits. Require a DONE line (`rc=stopped`, `rc=crash`, `rc=append-error`) on every exit path for each version whose log ps-run-layer still owns. Add matrix rows for a version admitted at once while its log holds an earlier run's lines, and for a stop during wait-slots.

findings.location: Boundaries > Always (Child: `--slot-cost n` stamps psm.slots on the PS container only); Ask First
findings.issue: Only children started by ps-run-layer get --slot-cost. A direct `ps-e2e-run.py` run (SKILL.md Lapis 4, the e2e-quickstart TDD loop) boots a PS container with no psm.slots label, so the host-wide cap never counts it. The SPEC Constraints say the cap covers every running E2E container from every client of the daemon. The spec does not decide a default cost for direct runs or call the gap out. It also does not validate --slot-cost (0, negative, non-integer), does not say whether --run-id/--slot-cost/--progress-append are only valid together, and does not say what an unlabelled or malformed psm.slots value (for example 'x' or '0') counts as.
findings.implementation_impact: The documented quickstart loop silently bypasses the cap and causes exactly the wait-healthy saturation that CAP-3 targets. A malformed label from another client can raise an exception inside the counting code, or be skipped and under-count.
findings.suggestion: Decide explicitly: either direct E2E runs stamp psm.slots=1 by default (Layer 2/5 stay 0), or add the gap to Never/deferred-work with its rationale. Specify that --slot-cost must be an integer ≥ 1 (else exit 2), and that a non-integer or < 1 label value counts as the cap being full (or as 1). Add both cases to the Labels and Bad input rows.

findings.location: Boundaries > Always (`ps-run-layer.py --slots N`); Tasks > docs (`--jobs` -> `--slots`)
findings.issue: --slots is a per-invocation number that is checked against a daemon-wide sum. Two concurrent runs with different values (one with `--slots 1`, one with config 6) enforce different caps on the same daemon: the run with 6 admits while the sum is 5, and the run with 1 waits until it times out to no-slots. The docs task treats `--jobs` -> `--slots` as a rename. In run-phases.md, the advice to run one version per call with `--jobs 1` and the stall advice to 'turunkan --jobs' (lower --jobs) both have per-run meaning. Rewritten to `--slots 1`, they would make the operator's own run starve whenever any other E2E container exists anywhere on the daemon.
findings.implementation_impact: Following the mechanically renamed docs produces spurious no-slots records. Two CAP-1 sessions with mismatched slot values can drive each other to blocked-infra.
findings.suggestion: State in the docs task that --slots/psm_e2e_slots is a host-wide ceiling that every concurrent run should share. Replace the harness-without-background advice with 'one version per --cells call' (no --slots), and replace 'lower --jobs' with 'lower psm_e2e_slots in config for every session'. Optionally log a warning when a run's N differs from the psm.slots sum seen at admission.

findings.location: Boundaries > Always ('--jobs with layer e2e = exit 2 naming --slots'); Code Map `main` (`--jobs`/`--slots`)
findings.issue: ps-run-layer's argparse defines `--jobs` with `default=DEFAULT_JOBS` (3), so an explicit `--jobs` cannot be told apart from the default unless the default changes to None. The spec does not say this. It also does not say what happens with `--slots` or `--jobs` under `--merge-only --layer e2e` (the previous slice ignores `--jobs` there), or whether an invalid `psm_e2e_slots` in --config is an error for Layer 2/5 runs that never read it.
findings.implementation_impact: A naive implementation rejects every e2e run, because args.jobs is always 3. Merge-only and Layer 2/5 config handling diverge between implementers, and the 'Bad input' row has no definitive expectation for these cases.
findings.suggestion: Specify `--jobs` default=None, resolved to DEFAULT_JOBS for Layers 2/5. Under `--merge-only --layer e2e`, either --slots/--jobs → exit 2 or both are ignored (pick one). psm_e2e_slots is validated only for non-merge layer e2e. Add those rows to the matrix.

findings.location: Tasks > ps-flashlight-run.py (`job_update(**fields)` rewriting the own registry entry); Design Notes > Claims
findings.issue: Claims live in ps-run-layer's registry JSON, which other processes read while counting. The spec does not require atomic replacement (write a temp file, then rename). job_register's current write_text truncates the file and then writes it, and `_registry_entries` silently skips a file it cannot parse, so a reader that catches a half-written file drops that run's claims and over-admits. The spec also does not say whether claim removal after a reap takes slots.lock. When job_register fails to write the entry (OSError, entry_path None, today a silent pass), the run's claims are invisible to every other run, and the spec does not say whether that should abort the run or degrade it.
findings.implementation_impact: There is an intermittent cap breach under concurrent runs that tests with stubs will never catch. A read-only or full /tmp turns the host-wide cap into a per-run cap with no signal to the operator.
findings.suggestion: Require job_update and job_register to write a sibling temp file and os.replace it. Require claim add and remove under slots.lock. Make failure to persist a claim an exit 2 before any spawn (or a stderr warning plus fallback to admitting one cell at a time; pick one). Add a test where a corrupt or partial entry is present.

findings.location: Tasks > tests ('harness stubs daemon_slot_usage, cleanup_orphans and points JOB_REGISTRY/lock dir at a temp dir'); Acceptance Criteria #2
findings.issue: AC2 requires two ps-run-layer runs that share one registry, with a visible 'ALIVE wait-slots' line naming the claim. The existing harness runs ps-run-layer in-process with injected runners. Two in-process runs share the module-global `_JOB` (one entry_path), `RUN_ID`, OWNER_PID and `_PROGRESS`, so the second run's job_register/job_update overwrites the first run's entry bookkeeping. Running them as two processes means the stubs (daemon_slot_usage, cleanup_orphans) cannot be monkeypatched and need an env-var or file hook, which the spec does not define. ALIVE lines come every PROGRESS_HEARTBEAT (15 s), and the spec gives no injectable heartbeat or poll interval, so the test either sleeps for at least 15 s or cannot observe the line.
findings.implementation_impact: AC2 is either untestable as specified or forces ad hoc test-only globals that the reviewer cannot check against the spec. The suite slows down by tens of seconds per wait-slots test.
findings.suggestion: Specify the mechanism. Either the second 'run' is a real subprocess with stubs enabled through a documented test env var (for example PSM_TEST_SLOT_STUB=<json file>), or the AC is restated as a pre-seeded registry entry with a live claim (pid = test process) plus one in-process run. Make the heartbeat and admission poll intervals module constants that the tests override (for example 0.05 s).

findings.location: Boundaries > Always (Slots: admission under slots.lock); Code Map ps-run-layer slot admission loop
findings.issue: The spec does not give an admission poll interval, and it does not say whether slots.lock is held during the `docker ps` count, which can take up to DOCKER_CMD_TIMEOUT (120 s). If the lock is held across a slow or hung count, every ps-run-layer on the host blocks on the lock for up to 2 minutes per attempt. A blocking flock with no timeout also means a hung holder freezes every other run's admission, and that time is not counted toward their startup timeout. It also leaves undefined whether the ALIVE detail (counted containers and claims) is recomputed on every poll or frozen at the first attempt, even though AC2 expects the line to name the current claim.
findings.implementation_impact: A slow daemon (the exact condition CAP-3 targets) serializes every run's admission behind one docker call, and wait-slots durations measure lock contention instead of slot availability.
findings.suggestion: Specify a poll interval (for example 5 s). Under the lock, either take the docker snapshot with a short timeout, or take the snapshot outside the lock and re-validate it with only the registry read and the claim write inside. Acquire flock with a bounded retry so the wait counts toward wait-slots. Recompute the ALIVE detail on every poll.

findings.location: Boundaries > Always (no-slots: 'counted containers (psm.job@host=cost) in errors'); Acceptance Criteria #2 ('ALIVE wait-slots lines naming the claim')
findings.issue: The no-slots record and the ALIVE lines must list what fills the cap. The spec lists containers only, but live registry claims of other runs (whose containers are not running yet) also count, and the AC itself expects the claim to be named. For a failed docker count ('Count error' row), the spec does not say what goes into `errors`. The record could end up saying no-slots with an empty or misleading list and no docker error text.
findings.implementation_impact: The operator cannot tell which foreign job to clean or stop. Contract Config keys says the list exists precisely so that a foreign orphan can be cleaned from its owner. The Count-error case is undiagnosable.
findings.suggestion: Define the errors/ALIVE payload as containers `psm.job@host=cost` plus claims `claim:<run>@<job>=cost`. When the count fails, use the docker error text (truncated) and 'count failed: treated as full'. Assert both in the Foreign full and Count error rows.

findings.location: Design Notes > Interim cost/mode; Never section
findings.issue: Every version runs with --sequential-browsers and no snapshot-db reset, but its records still carry `browser_mode: sequential`. The contract (Parallel browsers > Slots) defines sequential mode as resetting to a snapshot before each later engine. Records made in this slice are gate-grade and stay fresh until the source changes, so after CAP-7 lands they are indistinguishable from contract-conformant sequential evidence even though Firefox ran on a DB that Chromium had already mutated.
findings.implementation_impact: The honesty guarantee that 'each engine starts from the same state' is silently claimed by evidence that does not meet it. A residue-masked Firefox pass from this slice could satisfy `ready` after CAP-7 without a rerun.
findings.suggestion: Either stamp a marker (for example `browser_mode: sequential-shared-db`, or a note in `browser_notes`) that later readers treat as non-gate-grade once CAP-7 lands, or record in deferred-work that CAP-7 must stale pre-CAP-7 sequential records (for example via an evidence schema version in the fingerprint comparison).

findings.location: Tasks > docs (SKILL.md, run-phases.md, headless.md, README only); context companion spec-psm-e2e-cap2-cap6-cell-evidence.interim-orchestration.md
findings.issue: After this slice, a multi-version `--cells` run stops at the first fail and appends not-run records. The approved interim orchestration companion still says '--jobs as today' (Fase 2 step 3), which now exits 2. Its 'Run outcomes' classification knows only fail / inconclusive / inconclusive-steps / browser-notes, so the plan reason `not-run` has no defined handling. 'V's E2E step is due' is keyed on 'an E2E run of V printed the current source_fingerprint', which a run that left V not-run arguably satisfies, so V is never retried in the session. Headless callers (psm-develop, psm-cross-version, psm-optimize) lose per-version verdicts for not-run versions, and the CAP-1 `reached`/'not reached' handling that the contract uses to explain this is deferred. The docs task does not cover any of this.
findings.implementation_impact: The orchestrator either calls ps-run-layer with --jobs (exit 2, treated as a pre-spawn input error loop), or treats not-run versions as neither failed nor infra and stalls or reports them inconsistently. psm-optimize can misreport a not-run version as 'no new failure'.
findings.suggestion: Add a docs/companion task. Update the interim orchestration (or its successor text in run-phases.md/headless.md) to (a) use --slots, (b) classify reason `not-run` as 'not attempted: due again', with no-slots as an infra reason, and (c) exclude not-run cells from the 'printed the fingerprint' test. Tell headless callers that a version whose cells are all not-run is unproven, never a pass or a per-version finding.

findings.location: Boundaries > Always (Child: `--sequential-browsers` engine fail-fast; 'ps-run-layer copies a child-emitted not-run cell into the record as is')
findings.issue: 'As is' conflicts with the existing build_record path. Today every cell that has child data goes through derive_state, which turns a never-driven cell into `inconclusive/not-driven`. The spec does not say which fields ps-run-layer still fills or overrides for such a cell (started_at/finished_at null -> admission/write time, phase_durations with merged wait-slots, session, fingerprint, job_id, image_tag). It also does not say which state the child uses to decide 'fail' in the middle of the loop. If the child judges fail from findings alone, while version-level errors or install would make ps-run-layer's merged record inconclusive, then firefox ends up not-run 'after 9.1:chromium' while the chromium record is not a fail, and the run-level trigger never fires.
findings.implementation_impact: Records can name a trigger cell whose own record is not `fail`, which breaks the not-run invariant in cell-contract.md and confuses the plan's focus-cell logic in CAP-1.
findings.suggestion: Specify that the child decides an engine's fail with cell_state (the same derive_state over the merged version-level errors/install). Specify that ps-run-layer skips derive_state only for cells with `state: not-run` and a reason matching `^fail-fast after `, keeps their state, conclusive and reason, and fills the run-level fields and timestamps as for any record without an engine. Add a test where a not-run cell from the child round-trips into history unchanged except for those fields.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap3-failfast-slots.md:26 (Always > Slots, `--jobs` with layer e2e = exit 2)
findings.issue: `--jobs` has argparse default DEFAULT_JOBS=3 today, so 'given' cannot be told apart from the default; the spec does not say how explicit use is detected.
findings.implementation_impact: Either every e2e run exits 2 (default counted as given) or an explicit `--jobs 3` slips through silently.
findings.suggestion: State: `--jobs` default becomes None; layer e2e with `args.jobs is not None` exits 2; other layers resolve None to DEFAULT_JOBS.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap3-failfast-slots.md:26 (Slots input rules) / Code Map `main`
findings.issue: Not specified how `--slots` is treated with `--merge-only --layer e2e` (which accepts only --module, --reports-dir, --config), or whether `--slots`/`--jobs` placed in the passthrough after `--` are rejected before spawning.
findings.implementation_impact: `--slots` may be silently ignored in merge-only mode; a passthrough `--slots`/`--jobs` reaches the child, which exits 2. That child-originated exit 2 ends the E2E loop instead of the run failing before spawn.
findings.suggestion: Add `--slots` to the merge-only e2e rejection list and to RESERVED_PASSTHROUGH (and `--jobs`), both exit 2 pre-spawn.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap3-failfast-slots.md:26,48 (`psm_e2e_slots` from --config, Bad input row)
findings.issue: Config value forms are left unspecified: empty string "", a JSON number 6, "6.0", " 6 ", or a boolean. Also unspecified: whether a bad config value is still an error when `--slots` is given explicitly, or when the layer is not e2e.
findings.implementation_impact: Implementations can disagree: empty string treated as the default or as exit 2, an invalid config rejected or ignored when the flag wins, and non-e2e runs failing on an E2E-only key.
findings.suggestion: Specify: read only for layer e2e; empty/absent = default 6; accept str or int (not bool) parsed by int(); config validated even when --slots given (exit 2), mirroring psm_flashlight_startup_timeout handling.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap3-failfast-slots.md:26 (startup-timeout clock)
findings.issue: Not specified whether the no-slots clock resets or keeps accumulating each time an own child is reaped. Nor is it said whether the clock is per cell or per run.
findings.implementation_impact: Wait before `no-slots` can be shorter than the timeout (accumulated) or unbounded-ish across alternations (reset); test for Own queue row ambiguous.
findings.suggestion: Define one run-wide counter: accumulates only while own in-flight == 0 and a cell is waiting; never resets; no-slots when counter >= timeout.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap3-failfast-slots.md:26,43 (Foreign full `--startup-timeout 1`, admission polling)
findings.issue: No admission re-poll interval is specified. Nothing says how a single `docker ps` count call, which can block for DOCKER_CMD_TIMEOUT (120 s) or wait on slots.lock, interacts with a short startup timeout.
findings.implementation_impact: A timeout of 1s can overrun by up to 120s+lock wait; the timeout check may happen only between polls, making tests flaky or slow.
findings.suggestion: Specify poll interval (e.g. PROGRESS_HEARTBEAT or 5s) and that the deadline is checked after each count; a count that overruns the deadline yields no-slots immediately.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap3-failfast-slots.md:26 / 79 (Claims counted while no running container carries that psm.run)
findings.issue: owner_labels() also puts psm.run on the DB container (and the network). The DB container runs before the PS container that carries psm.slots, so for that window the claim stops counting while the cost is not yet visible.
findings.implementation_impact: A slot is counted as free during the window between the DB and PS containers starting. A concurrent run admits over the cap: the daemon is oversubscribed, which this slice exists to prevent.
findings.suggestion: Release a claim only when a running container carries BOTH `psm.run=<claim>` and a `psm.slots` label (docker ps --filter label=psm.run=X --filter label=psm.slots).

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap3-failfast-slots.md:26,79 (live registry `slot_claims`)
findings.issue: Not specified which entry_state values count as 'live' for claims. entry_state returns 'foreign' for another host or PID namespace sharing the temp dir, or for a bad pid.
findings.implementation_impact: Foreign entries sharing /tmp (e.g. bind-mounted tmp, containers) are either over-counted forever (stuck full) or ignored (oversubscription).
findings.suggestion: Specify: count claims only from entries whose entry_state is 'alive'; 'foreign' entries counted too (conservative) unless older than N; 'dead' never.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap3-failfast-slots.md:64 (`job_update(**fields)` rewriting own registry entry)
findings.issue: The spec does not require the registry rewrite to be atomic. Claim removal at reap may also happen outside slots.lock. `_registry_entries` silently skips unparseable JSON.
findings.implementation_impact: A concurrent reader sees a truncated entry. It counts zero claims and over-admits, or `--stop-job`/`--list-jobs` miss the process.
findings.suggestion: Require write to `<pid>.json.tmp` then os.replace; claim add and remove both performed under slots.lock.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap3-failfast-slots.md:26 (`slots.lock`)
findings.issue: No error path is specified for slots.lock: creating `<tmp>/psm-locks/` or opening the lock file can fail (permission denied in a shared multi-user /tmp, read-only tmp).
findings.implementation_impact: Unhandled OSError crashes ps-run-layer mid-run, or admission proceeds without the lock and races other runs.
findings.suggestion: Specify: lock OSError = treat as cap full (like count error) and log it, or input/env error exit 2 before spawning; pick one.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap3-failfast-slots.md:26 vs cell-contract.md Config keys (`--cleanup-orphans` timing)
findings.issue: This spec says cleanup runs 'once before the first admission'. The contract says 'before entering wait-slots'. The cleanup_orphans result status `partial`, an error, or an exception is also unhandled.
findings.implementation_impact: Cleanup either runs on every e2e run (even with free slots) or only on contention; a cleanup exception could abort the run before any record.
findings.suggestion: Pick one trigger explicitly (e.g. first time an admission attempt fails); cleanup failure is logged and ignored, never changes exit code.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap3-failfast-slots.md:25,39-40 (fail-fast trigger order)
findings.issue: 'Completion order' is undefined when several children are reaped in the same wait() batch: today's run_children sorts a batch by plan order. A fail and a child exit 2 can also be reaped together, or in either order.
findings.implementation_impact: The not-run reason (`fail-fast after X` vs `input-error after Y`) and the named cell are nondeterministic or follow plan order, contradicting the spec.
findings.suggestion: State: within one reap batch process in plan order; the first trigger processed fixes the reason for all not-run cells; exit 2 still wins the exit code if any child exited 2.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap3-failfast-slots.md:25,27 (`<ver>:<browser>` = first failing engine in psm_e2e_browsers order; sequential order)
findings.issue: The child does not reorder `--engines` (built from `--cells` order, e.g. `9.1:firefox+chromium`) into psm_e2e_browsers order. The spec does not say whether `--sequential-browsers` drives engines in `--engines` order or config order.
findings.implementation_impact: Child drives firefox first and fail-fasts chromium, while the contract says chromium (config order) runs first; named trigger browser may not match the engine that actually ran first.
findings.suggestion: Specify ps-run-layer (or child) sorts each version's engines by psm_e2e_browsers order before passing `--engines`.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap3-failfast-slots.md:27 (`--sequential-browsers` not-run cells)
findings.issue: The spec does not say what happens to an engine that is both unavailable (binary probe drop) and after the failing engine. Its cell could be child-emitted `not-run` or ps-run-layer-derived `browser-unavailable`.
findings.implementation_impact: Inconsistent records for the same situation; a child-emitted not-run hides the browser-unavailable diagnosis.
findings.suggestion: Specify precedence: child emits not-run only for engines in its usable list; unusable engines stay absent and get browser-unavailable.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap3-failfast-slots.md:27,31 (`--sequential-browsers` on direct multi-version runs)
findings.issue: Not specified whether a direct `ps-e2e-run.py --versions a,b --sequential-browsers` stops later versions after a version's fail, or only later engines within that version.
findings.implementation_impact: Direct runs may unexpectedly skip whole versions or not; tests and docs diverge.
findings.suggestion: State: engine fail-fast is per version only; the child never skips versions (version fail-fast is ps-run-layer's).

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap3-failfast-slots.md:27 (child `--slot-cost`, `--run-id` validation)
findings.issue: No validation rule is given for `--slot-cost`: 0, negative, or non-integer values, `--slot-cost` without `--run-id`, or the reverse.
findings.implementation_impact: A child could stamp `psm.slots=0`/`-1` (undercounting the daemon cap) or crash on int parsing with rc 1 instead of 2.
findings.suggestion: Specify: `--slot-cost` int >= 1 else exit 2; both flags optional and independent (direct runs omit both and stamp no label).

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap3-failfast-slots.md:25,27 (child exit 2 before progress_init)
findings.issue: An invalid `--run-id` makes the child exit 2 before progress is set, so run_main_with_progress writes no DONE line. The spec does not say whether ps-run-layer writes DONE for that version.
findings.implementation_impact: That version's log ends without DONE, which monitors read as a hung run.
findings.suggestion: Specify ps-run-layer appends `DONE rc=2` (input-error) to the version log after reaping a child exit 2 when the log lacks a DONE line.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap3-failfast-slots.md:25 (fail-fast on append error)
findings.issue: Unspecified: a `fail` record whose history append fails (append_error). It is unclear whether fail-fast fires (nothing was appended) and whether unstarted cells still get not-run records while appends are failing.
findings.implementation_impact: Queued cells either keep booting after a known fail or silently get no record; exit 2 without output line hides which cells ran.
findings.suggestion: State: append_error stops admission like fail-fast; not-run records are attempted with reason of the trigger; exit stays 2 as today.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap3-failfast-slots.md:25,29 (own `--stop-job` while cells queued or in wait-slots)
findings.issue: The spec gives no behavior for the run's own stop (JobStopped) while versions are queued or waiting in wait-slots. It is unclear whether their logs get a DONE line and whether their claims or wait-slots phase are closed. `stopped` records are out of scope, and not-run is not said to apply.
findings.implementation_impact: Waiting versions' logs keep START wait-slots/ALIVE lines with no END/DONE; registry claims may linger until process exit.
findings.suggestion: Specify: on JobStopped no records for unstarted cells; each truncated-but-unspawned version log gets `END wait-slots stopped` (if open) and `DONE rc=stopped`.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap3-failfast-slots.md:25,80 (cancelled wait-slots)
findings.issue: No outcome is given for a wait-slots phase that fail-fast cancels: success is `ok` and timeout is `no-slots`, but cancellation has no value. It is also unclear whether a not-run record whose wait was cancelled keeps `phase_durations.wait-slots`, given its log is truncated to one DONE line.
findings.implementation_impact: Records carry arbitrary outcome strings or drop the measured wait; log and record disagree.
findings.suggestion: Specify outcome `cancelled` and keep `{"wait-slots": {seconds, outcome: "cancelled"}}` in the not-run record.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap3-failfast-slots.md:26,80 (no-slots for every still-queued cell)
findings.issue: For versions queued behind the timed-out head that never entered wait-slots themselves, the spec does not say whether their log gets START/END wait-slots or a single `DONE rc=no-slots` line. It also leaves open whether their phase_durations hold the head's wait-slots or null.
findings.implementation_impact: Inconsistent logs and phase_durations across no-slots records of one run; aggregate e2e_phase_durations misleading.
findings.suggestion: Specify: only the waiting version records wait-slots; other queued versions get truncated log `DONE rc=no-slots` and phase_durations null.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap3-failfast-slots.md:26,45 (no-slots `errors` on Count error)
findings.issue: `errors` must list the counted containers (`psm.job@host=cost`), but the spec does not say what goes there when the docker count itself failed and nothing was counted.
findings.implementation_impact: A no-slots record with empty `errors` hides that the cap was never measured; diagnosing a broken daemon becomes impossible.
findings.suggestion: Specify: on count failure `errors` holds `docker count failed: <stderr tail>` (plus live claims), never empty.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap3-failfast-slots.md:79-80 (records without a child: started_at/finished_at/image_tag)
findings.issue: The spec does not set `started_at` for not-run and no-slots records. build_record falls back to `admitted[ver]`, which never exists for an unadmitted version. `finished_at` and `wall_clock` are also undefined for them.
findings.implementation_impact: KeyError in ps-run-layer or records with null timestamps that fail the incomplete-record rule.
findings.suggestion: Specify: started_at = when the version was first queued/attempted (run start), finished_at = when the record is written, wall_clock = difference.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap3-failfast-slots.md:80 (wait-slots merge into spawned version's records)
findings.issue: The spec covers merging wait-slots into child-emitted cells. It does not cover crash or browser-unavailable records of a version that waited (child spawned, no usable cell).
findings.implementation_impact: The measured wait is lost for exactly the records that need diagnosis; inconsistent phase_durations.
findings.suggestion: State: every record of a spawned version (crash/browser-unavailable included) gets the wait-slots entry; phase_durations = {wait-slots} when no child cell exists.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap3-failfast-slots.md:29 vs cell-contract.md Runner > Output (skipped child + not-run/no-slots)
findings.issue: The spec's honesty law says exit 1 if any record is not `pass`. The contract says any child `skipped` with no `fail` gives `skipped`, exit 0. The two conflict when not-run or no-slots records are also appended.
findings.implementation_impact: A run with no-slots cells may exit 0 `skipped`, letting the loop end as if nothing were unproven, or exit 1 contradicting the contract.
findings.suggestion: State precedence explicitly: exit2 > fail(3) > skipped(0) > any non-pass(1), or have no-slots/not-run override skipped to 1.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap3-failfast-slots.md:26 (`--startup-timeout` value)
findings.issue: Startup-timeout values of 0 or below (from the passthrough or `psm_flashlight_startup_timeout`) are not validated, and their effect on the no-slots clock is undefined.
findings.implementation_impact: `--startup-timeout 0` gives immediate no-slots for every cell on any contention; negative values behave arbitrarily.
findings.suggestion: Specify: startup timeout must be int >= 1 else exit 2, validated before spawning.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap3-failfast-slots.md:73 (AC: `ALIVE wait-slots` lines naming the claim)
findings.issue: The heartbeat format is undefined. The AC requires naming 'the claim' (which identifier: run id, job, pid?). The contract requires counted containers as `psm.job`@host.
findings.implementation_impact: AC test cannot be written deterministically; implementation may name containers only and fail the AC.
findings.suggestion: Define the line: `ALIVE wait-slots <n>s used=<u>/<slots> containers=<job@host=cost,...> claims=<job:run=cost,...>`.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap3-failfast-slots.md:26 / cell-contract Runner > Output (Docker becomes absent mid-run)
findings.issue: Docker being absent is checked once before counting (gives `skipped`). The spec does not say whether `daemon_slot_usage` tells a missing docker binary or daemon apart from a failed call when this happens on a later admission.
findings.implementation_impact: Docker vanishing mid-run yields no-slots records (inconclusive) rather than skipped, or vice versa, depending on implementation.
findings.suggestion: State: docker_available() checked only once before the first admission; every later count failure (including absent daemon) = cap full.

findings.location: Boundaries > Always (Fail-fast bullet) + Design Notes > Trigger vs cell-contract.md > Runner (Fail-fast bullet)
findings.issue: The spec says fail-fast fires when a reaped child has appended a `fail` record. The contract says it fires on 'the first child that exits 3'. Design Notes adds that an exit-3 child whose output crashed does not trigger. That changes a contract rule, but the Approach paragraph says the contract is authoritative for 'Runner > fail-fast', and Ask First requires asking before 'changing a contract rule rather than deferring it'. No approval is recorded.
findings.implementation_impact: Two rules give different results when a child exits 3 with unparseable output (all its cells `crash`). The spec says the queue keeps running; the contract says the queue stops. A test for that case passes under one reading and fails under the other, and the implementer cannot ask which one wins.
findings.suggestion: Either record the trigger change as an approved interim decision (and update cell-contract.md Runner > Fail-fast to 'first appended `fail` record'), or revert to 'first child that exits 3'. Add an I/O row: exit-3 child with crashed output -> fail-fast or not, stated explicitly.

findings.location: Design Notes > Records without a child ('`wait-slots` is recorded only when the first admission attempt failed'; 'a `no-slots` version's log ends `END wait-slots no-slots`') + Always (Slots bullet)
findings.issue: The spec never says which queued versions attempt admission and when. Option 1: only the queue head attempts (FIFO), so later versions have no wait-slots phase yet. Option 2: every queued version attempts at start and enters wait-slots at once. The two notes need different options. Under FIFO, the versions behind the head never START wait-slots, yet on timeout they get `no-slots` and their log must end `END wait-slots no-slots`, and their `phase_durations` must be either `{wait-slots}` or `null`.
findings.implementation_impact: The implementer must guess the queue model. The guess decides each queued version's progress log content, whether its `phase_durations.wait-slots` exists and how long it is, and how many ALIVE heartbeats run at once. The no-slots I/O rows cannot be asserted exactly.
findings.suggestion: State the model, e.g. 'every queued version enters `wait-slots` (START line + heartbeat) at the first admission pass when it cannot be admitted; admission order is queue order (the `--cells` written order)'. Alternatively, say what a never-attempted version gets in its log and its `phase_durations` on no-slots and on not-run.

findings.location: Always (Slots bullet: 'startup-timeout clock counts only while none of this run's own children is in flight; timeout -> `no-slots` ... for every still-queued cell') vs cell-contract.md > Config keys (`psm_e2e_slots` sub-bullet: 'the cell waits ... for at most the startup timeout')
findings.issue: The clock is not fully defined. (a) Is it one per run or one per cell? The contract wording is per cell; the spec implies one run-wide clock. (b) When an own child finishes, does the clock resume from its accumulated value or reset to 0? (c) Is time spent before any own child was admitted counted? (d) How often does ps-run-layer re-count while waiting? The poll interval is not given.
findings.implementation_impact: Example: `--slots 2`, a foreign run uses 1 slot, own version A runs, B and C wait. After A finishes, B may time out immediately or get a fresh 180 s, depending on the reading. 'Own queue' and 'Foreign full' cover only the extremes, so the in-between behaviour is guessed and untested.
findings.suggestion: Define it: 'one run-wide accumulator that advances only while no own child is in flight and the cap is full; it never resets; when it reaches the timeout, every still-queued cell gets `no-slots`'. Give the recount interval as a named constant tests can patch. Add an I/O row for a run that waits, admits, then waits again.

findings.location: Always (child `--progress-append`) + cell-contract.md > Phase timings ('ps-run-layer truncates the version's progress log before [wait-slots]') + docs task (run-phases.md 'Diduga macet', headless.md 'Log diam ±3 menit tanpa DONE')
findings.issue: Every child now gets `--progress-append` and never truncates. The spec never says when ps-run-layer truncates the log of a version that is admitted without waiting: at run start, or at admission? Separately, a queued version that has not started waiting (FIFO), or that waits behind its own run's cells for hours, may have an empty or stale log with no `DONE`. The current monitoring rules ('mtime unchanged ±3 min and no DONE = suspected hang'; headless: '--stop-job and return `blocked`') would then stop a correctly queued run. The docs task does not update those rules.
findings.implementation_impact: Without truncation, a version admitted on the first try keeps lines from an earlier run. Headless callers would kill healthy runs that are queued under `--slots`, which is exactly the 'Own queue' scenario.
findings.suggestion: Specify: 'ps-run-layer truncates every version's log once before the first admission pass'. Require that every unadmitted version emits ALIVE lines at least every PROGRESS_HEARTBEAT, or write a `QUEUED` token. Add to the docs task: update the silent-log hang rules in run-phases.md, SKILL.md 'Pantau run Docker' and headless.md for `wait-slots` and queued versions.

findings.location: Tasks > ps-flashlight-run.py (progress helper) + docs task ('`wait-slots` ... never `SLOW`') vs ps-flashlight-run.py `phase` class / `PROGRESS_SLOW_AFTER_PHASE` / `_PROGRESS`
findings.issue: `fl.phase` writes through the global `_PROGRESS` path and version, runs its heartbeat thread with the global `progress()`, records into the global timing sink, and marks SLOW after 180 s, because `PROGRESS_SLOW_AFTER_PHASE` has no entry for `wait-slots` and `_PROGRESS['slow_after']` overrides it anyway. The code tasks add only a path+version `progress` helper. Nothing provides a per-version heartbeat, the SLOW exemption the contract names ('`PROGRESS_SLOW_AFTER_PHASE` exempts them'), or the `{seconds, outcome}` timing for a phase run inside ps-run-layer. The `outcome` value for a wait cancelled by fail-fast (or ended by exit 2 or a stop) is also undefined. Only 'no-slots' is implied, and 'ok' presumably for an admitted version.
findings.implementation_impact: Reusing `fl.phase` writes ALIVE lines to the wrong log (or to none, since ps-run-layer never calls `progress_init`), emits SLOW after 3 minutes, and breaks when several versions wait at once. The implementer must design a new heartbeat or phase API without guidance and invent outcome strings.
findings.suggestion: Add a flashlight task item: a path+version-aware wait-phase helper (START/ALIVE/END, never SLOW, returns `{seconds, outcome}`). Add the exemption to `PROGRESS_SLOW_AFTER_PHASE` (or an explicit never-slow set) that the `slow_after` override cannot defeat. Enumerate the outcomes, e.g. `ok`, `no-slots`, `fail-fast`, `input-error`, `stopped`.

findings.location: Acceptance Criteria #2 ('`ALIVE wait-slots` lines naming the claim') + Always ('counted containers (`psm.job`@host=cost) in `errors`') vs cell-contract.md > Config keys (lines and record 'list the counted containers by `psm.job` and owner host')
findings.issue: The contract has ALIVE lines and the `no-slots` record name counted containers. The acceptance criterion requires the lines to name a claim, which is not a container. No format is given for a claim: run id, job id, pid, or cost? Also undefined: what `errors` holds when the cap is full only because of claims (no containers), and when the docker count failed ('Count error' row: counted list empty).
findings.implementation_impact: The AC2 assertion cannot be written without inventing a format. A `no-slots` record caused by another run's claims, or by a docker failure, would carry an empty `errors` list. That record explains nothing, yet `errors` drives the reason/inconclusive classification elsewhere.
findings.suggestion: Define one line/record vocabulary, e.g. containers `psm.job@host=cost` and claims `claim:<job>/<run>=cost`, plus a fixed string such as `docker-count-failed: <stderr tail>` for a failed count. State that `errors` lists both kinds.

findings.location: Tasks > ps-flashlight-run.py `daemon_slot_usage() -> (used, counted list, ok)` + Design Notes > Claims ('counted while no running container carries that `psm.run`')
findings.issue: To decide whether a claim still counts, the runner needs the `psm.run` of each running slot-labelled container. The return shape does not say the counted list carries `psm.run`. `owner_labels()` also stamps `psm.run` on the DB container and the network. A check against 'any running container carrying `psm.run`' would therefore drop the claim as soon as the DB starts, while the PS container is still being created behind `depends_on: service_healthy`. The cap would be over-admitted for the whole DB health wait. Also unspecified: a `psm.slots` label value that is not a positive integer (foreign or corrupt).
findings.implementation_impact: An implementer who queries `docker ps --filter label=psm.run=<id>` reintroduces the over-admission the claims exist to prevent. The result is a silent race on the shared daemon that no stubbed test catches.
findings.suggestion: Specify the counted-list entry as `{job, host, run, cost}`. State that a claim is released only by a counted entry (a running container labelled `psm.slots`) with the same `run`. Define how invalid `psm.slots` values are handled: count as 1, or treat the cap as full.

findings.location: Tasks > ps-flashlight-run.py `job_update(**fields)` + Design Notes > Claims ('removed when its child is reaped') vs `job_register`/`_registry_entries` in ps-flashlight-run.py
findings.issue: `job_register` writes the entry with a non-atomic `write_text`, and `_registry_entries` silently skips an unparseable file. The spec does not require `job_update` to replace the file atomically, nor that removing a claim after a reap happens under `slots.lock`. It also never says how admission recognises 'a live ps-run-layer registry entry'. Children register under the same job directory with `layer: e2e`, and `script` is `Path(sys.argv[0]).name`, which in the in-process harness is the test file, not `ps-run-layer.py`.
findings.implementation_impact: Another run that reads during a rewrite sees a torn file, skips it, and does not count its claims, so two runs over-admit. Choosing the 'ps-run-layer entry' marker by script name fails in tests; choosing by presence of `slot_claims` is a guess.
findings.suggestion: Require tmp-file + `os.replace` for `job_update`, and require claim add/remove while holding `slots.lock`. State that any live entry with a `slot_claims` list counts, whatever its script.

findings.location: Tasks > ps-e2e-run.py (`--sequential-browsers` engine fail-fast) + Code Map (`_run_one_version_inner` engine loop, `cell_state`)
findings.issue: Inside `_run_one_version_inner`, `cell['phase_durations']` stays `{}` until `run_one_version` copies the timing sink after the inner function returns. `derive_state` (via `cell_state`) treats a cell without `browser:<engine>` in `phase_durations` as `not-driven`. So `cell_state` called mid-loop always returns `inconclusive` and never `fail`.
findings.implementation_impact: If engine fail-fast follows the Code Map literally, it never fires. The 'Sequential child' row fails, or the implementer quietly invents another fail test that may diverge from the State rule.
findings.suggestion: State how the per-engine `fail` is decided mid-loop: e.g. copy the sink's `browser:<engine>` entry into the cell right after each engine, before calling `cell_state`. Or decide `fail` from `findings` non-empty plus no launch_error, errors or install failure, and say this must equal `derive_state`.

findings.location: Always (Child bullet: 'ps-run-layer copies a child-emitted `not-run` cell into the record as is') vs ps-run-layer.py `build_record` / `CELL_KEYS` / `RECORD_KEYS` and ps-e2e-run.py `_new_cell`
findings.issue: `build_record` takes only `CELL_KEYS`, which excludes `state`, `conclusive` and `reason`, and always recomputes state with `derive_state`, which would give `inconclusive`/`not-driven`. The spec says neither which fields 'as is' covers nor whether the child sets `conclusive: false`; the contract requires it. `_new_cell` defaults (`scenario_set: 'full'`, `browser_notes: []`, `phase_durations: {}`) would land in a cell that never ran, while the contract says fields no engine produced are `null`. Also unclear: whether the version's `wait-slots` entry is merged into a child not-run cell, and which version-level `boot_phases` and `install` it carries.
findings.implementation_impact: Different readings produce records that differ in state or reason, in `scenario_set`, and in `phase_durations`. The aggregate and plan read these, and a `scenario_set: full` not-run cell is misleading.
findings.suggestion: Spell it out. The child emits `state: not-run`, `conclusive: false`, `reason`, and `null` for every per-cell field, and `scenario_set` must be null. ps-run-layer takes `state`, `conclusive` and `reason` from such a cell without `derive_state`, copies version-level fields as for other cells, and merges `wait-slots` into its `phase_durations`.

findings.location: Design Notes > Records without a child (`run_id` = ps-run-layer's own) vs cell-contract.md > Evidence record > Fields ('`run_id` = RUN_ID of the version process') and ps-run-layer.py `build_record` (crash path uses `ctx['run_id']`)
findings.issue: A child now runs under the claim's pre-generated id (`--run-id`). When it crashes or produces unparseable output, a child did run, so by the contract the record's `run_id` should be the claim id. Today's code writes ps-run-layer's RUN_ID, and the spec only defines `run_id` for 'records without a child' (not-run and no-slots).
findings.implementation_impact: Crash and browser-unavailable records will point at the wrong process unless the implementer infers the change. Correlating a crash record with the child's progress log (`run=` field) and container labels becomes impossible.
findings.suggestion: Add: 'for an admitted version whose child left no usable output, `run_id` = that version's claim id'.

findings.location: Always (Child bullet `--slot-cost n`) + SPEC.md Constraints ('counted over every running E2E container ... from every client of the daemon')
findings.issue: A container is counted only when its process got `--slot-cost`. The spec gives no default for direct `ps-e2e-run.py` runs (SKILL.md Lapis 4, quickstart TDD loop) or for older callers, so their PS containers are unlabelled and invisible to the cap. It also does not say how `--slot-cost` is validated (0, negative, non-integer), or whether it is reserved for ps-run-layer callers only.
findings.implementation_impact: Direct E2E runs saturate the daemon while ps-run-layer believes slots are free, contradicting the SPEC's 'every running E2E container' constraint. Input validation for the new flag is guessed.
findings.suggestion: Decide: either direct runs stamp `psm.slots=1` by default (then say so and test it), or record the exemption explicitly as an interim gap. Add an input-error rule: `--slot-cost` must be an integer >= 1, else exit 2.

findings.location: I/O row 'Labels' ('`--slot-cost 2` compose / manual; Layer 2 boot: `psm.slots` sums 2 / 2 / 0') + Tasks > ps-flashlight-run.py ('slot-cost label on the PS container only')
findings.issue: `_compose_file_text`, `_compose_labels_yaml` and `_bring_up_manual_inner` are shared with Layer 2, and their signatures carry no cost. The spec does not say how the value gets from ps-e2e-run `main` to them: a module global like `_JOB`, or a new parameter. With `daemon_slot_usage` stubbed and no Docker in the harness, 'sums 2/2/0' has no defined measurement: generated compose text, captured `docker run` argv, or a mocked `docker ps` parse.
findings.implementation_impact: The done-criterion for this row is not mechanically testable as written. The plumbing choice affects whether Layer 2 can ever accidentally inherit a cost.
findings.suggestion: Specify the plumbing, e.g. `fl.SLOT_COST = None` set by ps-e2e-run only, and the test method: parse the generated compose YAML and the captured manual `docker run` argv, then sum `psm.slots` across the PS, DB and network artefacts.

findings.location: Always (Slots bullet: '`--jobs` with layer `e2e` = exit 2 naming `--slots`') vs ps-run-layer.py `main` (`--jobs` default=DEFAULT_JOBS=3; `args.jobs < 1` check runs first)
findings.issue: With argparse defaulting `--jobs` to 3, an explicit `--jobs` cannot be told apart from the default. The spec does not say to change the default to None. Also undefined: `--jobs`/`--slots` with `--merge-only --layer e2e` (the previous slice said `--jobs` is ignored there), and which message wins for `--jobs 0 --layer e2e`.
findings.implementation_impact: A literal implementation either rejects every e2e run or never rejects one. Edge-case handling for the merge-only view is guessed.
findings.suggestion: State: `--jobs` default None (Layers 2/5 fall back to DEFAULT_JOBS); for layer e2e (run and `--merge-only`) any `--jobs` is exit 2 naming `--slots`; `--slots` with `--merge-only` is exit 2.

findings.location: Always (Slots bullet: '`--cleanup-orphans` once before the first admission, every mode') vs SPEC.md Constraints / cell-contract.md > Config keys ('Before entering `wait-slots`') and the docs task ('automatic `--cleanup-orphans` before `wait-slots`')
findings.issue: The spec says before the first admission. The contract, the SPEC and the spec's own docs task say before entering wait-slots, which happens only when the cap is full. The spec also does not say what ps-run-layer does with the `cleanup_orphans()` result: log removed and skipped artefacts, treat `status: partial`/errors, or only log to stderr.
findings.implementation_impact: The implementer must pick one timing; tests that assert cleanup was or was not called on an uncontended run depend on the pick. Removed orphans may go unreported to the operator.
findings.suggestion: Pick one wording everywhere, e.g. 'once per run, after the Docker check and before the first slot count'. Specify a stderr summary line, and say that errors never fail the run.

findings.location: Acceptance Criteria #2 (two ps-run-layer runs sharing one registry, `--slots 1`)
findings.issue: The harness runs `main()` in-process. Two concurrent runs in one process share `_JOB`, `_PROGRESS`, the SIGTERM handler, `OWNER_PID` and the RUN_ID global, so the AC cannot be exercised that way. The second run is blocked only by another run's claim, so per the Slots bullet its startup-timeout clock runs, and it gets `no-slots` unless the first child is reaped before the timeout; the AC sets no timeout. ALIVE lines appear every 15 s (PROGRESS_HEARTBEAT). 'Lock dir' has no existing constant that the harness could point at a temp dir.
findings.implementation_impact: The AC is not testable as written. Depending on timing it contradicts the 'Foreign full' rule, and a naive test would take more than 15 s or flake.
findings.suggestion: Rewrite the AC. Simulate the first run with a hand-written registry entry holding a live PID (e.g. a sleeping subprocess whose cmdline matches) and a `slot_claims` entry; remove it within the startup timeout (`--startup-timeout` large); patch PROGRESS_HEARTBEAT. Name the new lock-dir constant (e.g. `fl.LOCK_DIR`).

findings.location: Always (Honesty law bullet: 'run exit 3 if any `fail`, else 1 if any record not `pass`') vs cell-contract.md > Runner > Output and the existing `run_e2e` exit logic
findings.issue: The exit rule leaves out three cases. (1) A child exit 2 forces exit 2 even when a `fail` exists. (2) A child reporting `status: skipped` gives `skipped` and exit 0 when no record is `fail`, even if not-run or no-slots records were appended. (3) A child stopped individually forces exit 1. Also undefined: a run with a skipped child plus `no-slots` cells. Is that exit 0 'skipped', which ends the E2E loop, or exit 1?
findings.implementation_impact: Implementing the bullet literally regresses exit-2 precedence and the skipped path. Implementing the existing logic leaves the skipped + no-slots combination to a guess.
findings.suggestion: Replace the bullet with the full precedence list: stop 143 > append error 2 (no line) > child exit 2 > any `fail` 3 > skipped 0 > any non-pass or stopped child 1 > 0. State explicitly how no-slots and not-run combine with skipped.

findings.location: Tasks > docs (SKILL.md, run-phases.md, headless.md) vs run-phases.md 'Istilah E2E' > Hasil run / Infra retry and spec-psm-e2e-cap2-cap6-cell-evidence.interim-orchestration.md (Fase 2 step 3 '`--jobs` as today')
findings.issue: The interim orchestration classifies run outcomes only by plan reasons `fail`, `inconclusive`, `inconclusive-steps` and `browser-notes`. A `no-slots` cell (plan reason `inconclusive`) triggers an 'infra retry' that asks Budi to fix the environment with examples (`--allow-image-pull`, `playwright install`), none of which fixes no-slots. A `not-run` cell (plan reason `not-run`) is not classified at all. The frozen interim companion still says '`--jobs` as today', and the docs task does not mention any of this.
findings.implementation_impact: Following the docs, the orchestrator mis-handles `no-slots` (asks for a useless fix; a decline ends the E2E loop) and has no rule for `not-run` cells. The implementer must invent orchestration text in a slice whose Never list excludes CAP-1.
findings.suggestion: Add to the docs task: in 'Hasil run', `not-run` means waiting on the triggering cell's fix (not due until the fingerprint changes); `no-slots` is an infra reason whose remedy is to wait, lower load, or `--cleanup-orphans`. Update the interim companion's `--jobs` mention, or state that the docs supersede it.

findings.location: Design Notes / resolve-psm-config task ('`DEFAULT_E2E_SLOTS = 6` in ps-run-layer with a drift check') vs tests/test-ps-flashlight-run.py drift block
findings.issue: The existing drift block lives in test-ps-flashlight-run.py, loads ps-flashlight-run as `mod`, and auto-enumerates only `psm_flashlight_*` keys. The spec names neither the file that hosts the new check nor how it reads a constant from ps-run-layer (`_literal_const` via ast, as for DEFAULT_BROWSERS?). It is also unclear whether `psm_e2e_slots` from `--config` is still validated (exit 2 on 'x') when an explicit `--slots` is given.
findings.implementation_impact: Minor guesses that decide test placement and an input-error edge case.
findings.suggestion: Name the test file and method (e.g. add a `_literal_const(ps-run-layer.py, 'DEFAULT_E2E_SLOTS')` check in test-ps-flashlight-run.py and a default assertion in test-resolve-psm-config.py). State whether `psm_e2e_slots` is validated when `--slots` is explicit.

findings.location: Always (child exit 2 bullet) + Tasks > ps-e2e-run.py (`--run-id` validated before progress)
findings.issue: The exit-2 version's log was truncated by ps-run-layer and may hold only wait-slots lines. A child that rejects `--run-id` exits 2 before `progress_init`, so no `DONE` is ever written. The same holds for queued versions when the run is stopped (`--stop-job`) during `wait-slots`. The spec defines DONE only for not-run and no-slots versions.
findings.implementation_impact: These logs end without `DONE` and look hung under the monitoring rules. The implementer must decide whether ps-run-layer writes e.g. `DONE rc=2` or `DONE rc=stopped` for them.
findings.suggestion: Specify the final line ps-run-layer writes for an exit-2 version whose log lacks DONE, and for unadmitted versions on stop.

findings.location: I/O row 'AC fail-fast' (`--cells 9.1:chromium,8.1:chromium,1.7.8:chromium`, '9.1 child fails ... 8.1 and 1.7.8 never spawned')
findings.issue: The row assumes 9.1 is admitted first. The spec never says whether the admission queue follows the `--cells` written order (as `parse_cells` keeps it) or the numeric version order.
findings.implementation_impact: If admission is sorted numerically, 1.7.8 runs first and the AC as written fails.
findings.suggestion: State: 'cells are queued in `--cells` written order (`--versions`: written order)'.

findings.location: Tasks > docs (SKILL.md/run-phases.md) vs run-phases.md 'Job ID' section ('Sisa run yang prosesnya sudah mati: `--cleanup-orphans`') and SKILL.md 'Hentikan hanya secara terarah'
